create.name: Village Zendo
create.bio:
The Village Zendo, also known by its Japanese temple name Dotoku-ji, is a Soto Zen community in lower Manhattan. It was started in 1986 by two teachers, Pat Enkyo O'Hara and Barbara Joshin O'Hara. Enkyo Roshi is a Dharma heir of Bernie Glassman, in the White Plum line that comes down from Taizan Maezumi, so the practice is Soto at heart with some Rinzai elements. She now serves as abbot emerita, many of the teachers she trained make up today's teaching circle, and Roshi Sinclair Shinryu Thomson is the current abbot.

The zendo, now on West Broadway in Tribeca, holds sitting meditation on weekday mornings and evenings, a Thursday Dharma talk and Sunday services with talks, and runs a parallel online zendo on Zoom with a Monday class for beginners and dedicated sitting groups. Through the year it offers monthly one-day retreats, an urban sesshin in March, and summer and winter practice periods with residential retreats outside the city. Members support the community with monthly dues and get priority for private meetings with teachers. Talks are shared as podcasts, transcripts and videos, and the community also brings Zen into the arts, writing and social action.

courses.title: Village Zendo Membership
courses.description: Monthly membership that supports the community and gives priority for private interviews with teachers, plus discounts on programmes and retreats. Anyone may join after an introductory conversation with a teacher; no one needs to be a member to sit with the sangha.
courses.price: $108 per month (distance members $65 per month; under 25 or over 70 $54 per month)

courses.title: Winter Sesshin: The Web of Interdependency
courses.description: The zendo's year-end residential retreat at the Garrison Institute in the Hudson Valley, with long periods of zazen, daily talks and individual meetings with teachers. A half-retreat option covers the first three days. Room and board are booked separately with the venue.
courses.price: Full retreat: Members $390, Non-Members $440; Half retreat: Members $195, Non-Members $225 (programme fees; room and board extra)

free_resources.title: Learn to Meditate
free_resources.description: A weekly online session on Monday evenings for newcomers and those wanting a refresher in Zen sitting. It covers posture, how to begin a regular practice and walking meditation, with time for questions.

free_resources.title: Online Zendo
free_resources.description: Twice-daily silent sitting on Zoom through the week, with Dharma talks on Thursday evenings and Sunday mornings. Open to anyone who keeps to the zendo's guidelines.

free_resources.title: Transcribed Talks
free_resources.description: Written versions of Dharma talks by the zendo's teachers, free to read online.
